E.fit: Not here: cross-reacts with HIT antibodies, worsening catastrophic thrombosis

Initiate non-heparin anticoagulant: IV direct thrombin inhibitor (argatroban or bivalirudin)
**Severe hepatic impairment present:** bivalirudin or fondaparinux preferred over argatroban

acute-kidney-injury.name: Acute kidney injury
acute-kidney-injury.core: Abrupt loss of renal filtration: separate impaired perfusion, parenchymal injury, and urinary obstruction before treating the cause.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Volume depletion, sepsis, heart failure, cirrhosis; baseline CKD increases vulnerability
NSAIDs constrict afferent arterioles; ACE inhibitors/ARBs reduce efferent tone during hypoperfusion
Aminoglycosides, pigment injury, prolonged ischemia → tubular damage; antibiotics/PPIs → interstitial inflammation

rows.label: Clues
items: Oliguria, edema, uremic nausea; urine output may remain normal
AIN: fever, rash, eosinophilia sometimes present; classic triad often absent
★ Pulmonary edema, severe hyperkalemia, encephalopathy, pericarditis → **urgent renal support**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Reduced glomerular pressure, tubular epithelial injury, or backpressure → declining GFR

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ AKI: creatinine ↑≥0.3 mg/dL within 48 h, ≥1.5-fold within 7 days, or oliguria
Oliguria criterion: urine <0.5 mL/kg/h for ≥6 h; trend creatinine, electrolytes, fluid balance
★ **Urinalysis + microscopy**, medication review; bladder scan → renal ultrasound if obstruction possible
FeNa unreliable with diuretics, CKD, early obstruction; urine eosinophils neither sensitive nor specific
Unexplained persistent injury or suspected glomerulonephritis → nephrology, possible kidney biopsy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Severe hyperkalemia → **IV calcium**, insulin/dextrose; refractory electrolyte disturbance → dialysis
Hypovolemia → isotonic crystalloid; congestion → loop diuretic; avoid reflex fluids in overloaded patients
Stop culprit nephrotoxins; renal-dose drugs; AIN persisting after withdrawal → consider glucocorticoids
★ Obstruction → **catheter or ureteral decompression**; monitor postobstructive diuresis
Dialysis: refractory acidosis, hyperkalemia, intoxication, overload, symptomatic uremia; no isolated creatinine threshold

rows.label: Complications
items: Arrhythmias, acidosis, volume overload; subsequent CKD
Recovery diuresis → dehydration and electrolyte losses

rows.label: Prevention
items: Maintain perfusion during illness; review nephrotoxic combinations and monitor renal function

rows.label: Mimics
items: CKD: longstanding abnormalities, small echogenic kidneys, chronic anemia
Trimethoprim effect: creatinine rise without true GFR decline

acute-kidney-injury.evidence: Not checked online; established KDIGO diagnostic criteria and renal teaching.

adult-immunizations.name: Adult immunizations
adult-immunizations.scope: Routine adult vaccines, immunocompromised and HIV, pregnancy, live-vaccine contraindications, chronic medical conditions (COPD, diabetes, liver disease), vaccine counseling and addressing hesitancy
adult-immunizations.core: Match vaccination to age, prior doses, pregnancy, immune status, and exposure risk; missed series resume without restarting.

rows.label: Who
items: ★ **HepB**: all adults 19–59; ≥60 with risk or requesting protection
Liver disease → HepA/HepB; COPD, diabetes, smoking → pneumococcal before routine age
Asplenia → pneumococcal, MenACWY, MenB, Hib; HIV → MenACWY

rows.label: Start/stop
items: ★ Pregnancy: **Tdap each pregnancy at 27–36 wk**; inactivated influenza any trimester
Maternal RSV: Abrysvo at 32–36 wk, September–January; previous pregnancy dose → infant antibody instead
RSV once: all ≥75; ages 50–74 with increased severe-disease risk

rows.label: Test
items: Review records, contraindications, immunity; HBV serology useful, but **do not delay vaccination**
★ Immunocompromised ≥19 → recombinant zoster; HIV CD4 ≥200 permits MMR/varicella if nonimmune
HPV started <15 → two doses; ≥15 or immunocompromised → three

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Avoid live MMR, varicella, intranasal influenza** during pregnancy or severe immunosuppression
PCV15 → PPSV23: minimum 8 weeks if immunocompromised; mild illness/antibiotics need no deferral
Hesitancy → elicit concern, explain benefit, recommend clearly; refusal → document, revisit

table.title: Routine adult schedule
rows: Annual influenza; updated COVID-19 for all adults
Tdap once, then either every 10 years
PCV20/21 alone; PCV15 → PPSV23 after 1 year

airway-management.name: Airway management
airway-management.scope: Indications for endotracheal intubation (GCS <= 8, airway protection, respiratory failure), rapid sequence intubation, bag-valve-mask ventilation, difficult airway
airway-management.core: Secure the airway when oxygenation, ventilation, or protection fails; preparation and rescue oxygenation determine safety.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Facial/neck trauma, burns, angioedema, obesity, limited jaw opening or cervical mobility
Shock, severe hypoxemia, metabolic acidosis increase peri-intubation collapse risk

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **GCS ≤8**, absent protective reflexes, recurrent aspiration, apnea → assess need for definitive airway
Stridor, fatigue, rising CO₂, refractory hypoxemia, inability to handle secretions → impending failure
GCS alone imperfect: reversible intoxication without ventilation/protection failure may permit closely monitored observation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Upper-airway obstruction, depressed drive, or respiratory muscle failure prevents effective gas exchange
Induction/positive pressure reduces sympathetic tone and venous return, worsening hypotension

rows.label: Dx
items: Continuous pulse oximetry, ECG, BP; assess mouth opening, neck anatomy, aspiration risk
★ Confirm tracheal placement with **persistent waveform capnography**, then auscultation and chest radiograph for depth
Do not rely on chest movement, oxygen saturation, or auscultation alone

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Position, suction, **preoxygenate**; prepare BVM, supraglottic device, video laryngoscope, and surgical rescue
Two-person BVM with airway adjunct and oxygen; oral adjunct only without gag reflex
RSI: etomidate/ketamine + rocuronium/succinylcholine; provide immediate postintubation analgesia and sedation
★ Predicted difficult airway → awake intubation strategy; **cannot intubate/cannot oxygenate → cricothyrotomy**
Avoid succinylcholine: hyperkalemia, denervation, established major burns, neuromuscular disease, malignant hyperthermia risk

rows.label: Complications
items: Esophageal/right-mainstem intubation, aspiration, dental injury, hypoxemia, cardiac arrest
Positive-pressure ventilation → barotrauma; prolonged ventilation → pneumonia, laryngeal injury

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Optimize **hemodynamics before induction**, use attempt limits and explicit backup plan
Head-of-bed elevation, oral care, daily sedation/ventilator liberation assessment

rows.label: Mimics
items: Panic hyperventilation: preserved oxygenation/protection, respiratory alkalosis
Compensatory Kussmaul breathing: metabolic acidosis; losing minute ventilation can cause abrupt deterioration

airway-management.evidence: Not checked online; established emergency airway principles.

alpha-1-antitrypsin-deficiency.name: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency
alpha-1-antitrypsin-deficiency.scope: SERPINA1 gene mutation (PiZZ phenotype), panacinar basilar emphysema in young nonsmokers, liver cirrhosis/hepatoma, PAS-positive diastase-resistant globules, serum AAT level and phenotype
alpha-1-antitrypsin-deficiency.core: Premature obstructive lung disease with unexplained liver disease or a family history suggests inherited alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Autosomal codominant **SERPINA1** variants; PiZZ phenotype causes severe deficiency
Smoking, secondhand smoke, occupational dust and fumes accelerate pulmonary injury

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Young nonsmoker with **basilar panacinar emphysema**, exertional dyspnea, and persistent airflow obstruction
Neonatal cholestasis or adult hepatic dysfunction; liver and lung disease may occur independently
Hyperinflation, diminished breath sounds; advanced disease → hypoxemia and right-heart strain

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Deficient circulating antiprotease → unopposed neutrophil elastase and alveolar wall destruction
Misfolded protein retained in hepatocyte endoplasmic reticulum → cellular injury, fibrosis

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Serum AAT level** → phenotype or genotype confirmation; acute inflammation can falsely elevate levels
Test all adults with COPD, unexplained bronchiectasis, or unexplained chronic liver disease
Spirometry establishes obstruction; chest CT defines distribution; LFTs and ultrasound assess hepatic injury
★ Liver biopsy, if obtained: **PAS-positive, diastase-resistant globules**; not required for routine diagnosis

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Smoking cessation** plus inhaled bronchodilators; pulmonary rehabilitation and oxygen for qualifying chronic hypoxemia
IV AAT augmentation for selected nonsmokers with severe deficiency and established emphysema; specialist selection
Augmentation does not treat liver injury; decompensated cirrhosis → liver transplantation
End-stage pulmonary disease despite treatment → lung transplantation evaluation

rows.label: Complications
items: Respiratory failure, pulmonary hypertension, recurrent respiratory infections
Cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma; hepatic cancer surveillance once cirrhosis develops

rows.label: Prevention
items: Offer genetic counseling and testing to first-degree relatives; genotype rather than level alone
Influenza, COVID-19, pneumococcal vaccines; hepatitis A/B vaccination with liver disease
Avoid excess alcohol and hepatotoxic exposures; monitor pulmonary function and liver tests

rows.label: Mimics
items: Smoking-related emphysema: predominantly upper-lobe centriacinar destruction
Cystic fibrosis: bronchiectasis, pancreatic insufficiency, elevated sweat chloride
Other cirrhosis: viral, alcohol, metabolic causes without the characteristic inherited pulmonary pattern

alpha-1-antitrypsin-deficiency.evidence: Not checked online; established AAT deficiency diagnosis and management.

anticoagulants.name: Anticoagulants
anticoagulants.scope: Warfarin (CYP interactions, INR monitoring, reversal with vitamin K and PCC), heparin and LMWH (protamine reversal, HIT), direct oral anticoagulants (apixaban, rivaroxaban, dabigatran, reversal agents)
anticoagulants.core: Anticoagulants prevent clot extension and embolization; drug choice depends on indication, renal function, pregnancy, and bleeding risk.

rows.label: Use
items: ★ **DOACs**: most nonvalvular AF and VTE; warfarin: mechanical valves, rheumatic mitral stenosis
LMWH: pregnancy; UFH: rapid reversibility or severe renal impairment

rows.label: Mechanism
items: Warfarin blocks vitamin K recycling → ↓II, VII, IX, X and proteins C/S
UFH/LMWH enhance antithrombin; UFH inhibits IIa/Xa, LMWH predominantly Xa
Apixaban/rivaroxaban directly inhibit Xa; dabigatran directly inhibits thrombin

rows.label: Adverse
items: Bleeding with all; warfarin → early skin necrosis, fetal injury
★ **HIT**: platelet fall >50%, usually days 5–10; thrombosis more characteristic than bleeding

rows.label: Avoid
items: Suspected HIT → stop every heparin source; start argatroban or another nonheparin anticoagulant
Warfarin initiation during acute HIT; DOACs for mechanical valves or high-risk antiphospholipid syndrome

rows.label: Interactions
items: Warfarin effect ↑ with amiodarone, TMP-SMX/metronidazole; ↓ with rifampin
DOAC exposure altered by strong P-glycoprotein/CYP3A modifiers; NSAIDs/antiplatelets increase bleeding

rows.label: Monitor
items: ★ Warfarin **INR**, usually 2–3; UFH aPTT/anti-Xa; LMWH/DOACs: renal function, CBC
No routine INR titration for DOACs; LMWH anti-Xa only selected situations

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Acute VTE warfarin → overlap parenteral anticoagulant ≥5 days and until therapeutic INR
Historical Xa antidote andexanet: US sales ended December 2025; use local PCC-based reversal protocols

aortic-dissection.name: Aortic dissection
aortic-dissection.core: Sudden maximal chest or back pain with vascular or neurologic deficits suggests aortic dissection, even without widened mediastinum.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Long-standing hypertension, bicuspid aortic valve, coarctation
Marfan/vascular Ehlers-Danlos, pregnancy, cocaine, aortic instrumentation or aneurysm

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Abrupt severe pain**, pulse/BP asymmetry, syncope, focal neurologic deficit
New aortic regurgitation murmur; limb ischemia or abdominal pain from branch-vessel malperfusion
Hypotension suggests rupture, tamponade, severe regurgitation, or coronary involvement

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Intimal tear → blood separates medial layers, creating false lumen
Propagation compromises branch arteries or ruptures into pericardium/pleura

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Stable → **CTA chest/abdomen/pelvis**; unstable or unable to leave resuscitation → bedside TEE
Chest radiograph may show widened mediastinum but normal film does not exclude dissection
ECG/troponin may mimic MI; high suspicion requires aortic imaging before antithrombotics
Examine bilateral arm pressures, femoral pulses, neurologic status, renal function

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **IV esmolol or labetalol** + opioid analgesia; target HR 60–80 and SBP <120 if perfusion maintained
Persistent hypertension after rate control → nicardipine; avoid vasodilator before beta blockade
★ **Avoid anticoagulation and thrombolysis** when dissection suspected
Tamponade from dissection → immediate surgical team; routine pericardiocentesis can worsen hemorrhage

rows.label: Complications
items: Aortic rupture, hemothorax, tamponade, MI, stroke, paraplegia, mesenteric/renal ischemia
Late aneurysmal dilation or recurrent dissection despite initial successful treatment

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Lifelong **BP control and surveillance CTA/MRA**; beta-blocker-based regimen
Avoid heavy isometric lifting; screen first-degree relatives for familial aortopathy

rows.label: Mimics
items: Acute coronary syndrome: pressure-like pain, no pulse deficit; coexistence possible
PE: pleuritic pain, hypoxemia, right-heart strain
Esophageal rupture: vomiting followed by pain and subcutaneous emphysema

aortic-dissection.evidence: Not checked online; established aortic emergency principles.

bowel-obstruction.name: Bowel obstruction
bowel-obstruction.scope: Small bowel obstruction (adhesions, hernia), large bowel obstruction (volvulus, malignancy), paralytic ileus, NG decompression, surgical management
bowel-obstruction.core: Colicky abdominal pain, vomiting, distention, and obstipation suggest mechanical obstruction; constant pain or systemic toxicity raises concern for strangulation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prior abdominal surgery, incarcerated hernia, Crohn strictures → small-bowel obstruction
Colorectal malignancy, chronic constipation, institutionalization → large-bowel obstruction or sigmoid volvulus
Recent surgery, opioids, hypokalemia, severe systemic illness → ileus

rows.label: Clues
items: Early high-pitched sounds may become absent; proximal obstruction causes earlier vomiting, distal disease greater distention
★ **Peritonitis, fever, tachycardia, rising lactate**, or continuous severe pain → ischemia/perforation
Partial obstruction may still permit stool or diarrhea; bowel movements do not exclude early obstruction

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Luminal blockage → upstream dilation, third spacing; closed loop compromises venous then arterial supply
Adynamic ileus reflects impaired motility without an anatomic transition point

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast** defines transition point, cause, and ischemic signs
CBC, electrolytes, creatinine, lactate; normal lactate cannot exclude early ischemia
Radiograph may show dilated loops/air-fluid levels; CT more definitive if diagnosis uncertain

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **NPO, IV isotonic fluids, electrolyte correction**; NG decompression for significant vomiting/distention
★ Strangulation, perforation, closed loop, or incarcerated hernia → **urgent surgery** + ceftriaxone/metronidazole
Uncomplicated adhesive SBO → surgical observation, serial examination; water-soluble contrast helps predict resolution
Failure to improve during a short monitored trial, commonly up to 72 h → operation
Ileus → correct trigger, reduce opioids, mobilize; no operation solely for absent sounds

rows.label: Complications
items: Dehydration, AKI, hypokalemic alkalosis; bowel necrosis, perforation, sepsis
Recurrent adhesions; short-bowel syndrome after extensive resection

rows.label: Prevention
items: Early postoperative ambulation, opioid-sparing analgesia, electrolyte correction; elective repair of symptomatic hernias

rows.label: Mimics
items: Gastroenteritis: prominent diarrhea, no focal transition point
Mesenteric ischemia: pain out of proportion before peritoneal signs

bowel-obstruction.evidence: Not checked online; established acute surgical management principles.

celiac-disease.name: Celiac disease
celiac-disease.scope: Gluten-sensitive enteropathy, malabsorption, iron deficiency anemia, dermatitis herpetiformis, IgA anti-tTG, small bowel villous atrophy, gluten-free diet
celiac-disease.core: Gluten-triggered autoimmune small-bowel injury causing malabsorption or unexplained iron deficiency, sometimes with intensely pruritic extensor-surface dermatitis herpetiformis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: First-degree relative, type 1 diabetes, autoimmune thyroid disease, selective IgA deficiency
HLA-DQ2/DQ8 susceptibility; positive genotype common and not diagnostic

rows.label: Clues
items: Chronic diarrhea, steatorrhea, bloating, weight loss; constipation or minimal GI symptoms possible
Iron deficiency refractory to oral replacement, aphthous ulcers, low bone density
Children: poor growth/delayed puberty; severe disease: hypoalbuminemia, edema, vitamin deficiencies

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Tissue transglutaminase modifies gliadin → T-cell response damages proximal intestinal mucosa
Impaired absorption → iron/folate/calcium deficiency; cutaneous granular IgA deposition causes rash

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ While **eating gluten → IgA anti-tTG + total IgA**; gluten restriction causes false negatives
★ IgA deficiency → **IgG anti-tTG or deamidated gliadin peptide antibodies**
★ Adults: positive serology or high suspicion → **EGD with multiple duodenal biopsies**, even if mucosa normal
Biopsy: villous atrophy, crypt hyperplasia, intraepithelial lymphocytes; high suspicion overrides negative serology

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Lifelong gluten-free diet**: avoid wheat, barley, rye; dietitian, cross-contamination counseling
Pure uncontaminated oats usually tolerated; replace iron, folate, calcium, vitamin D and other measured deficiencies
Dermatitis herpetiformis: dapsone for rapid relief after G6PD testing; diet treats underlying intestinal injury
Persistent symptoms → assess gluten exposure, alternative diagnoses; refractory disease → specialist before immunosuppression

rows.label: Complications
items: Osteoporosis, infertility; untreated disease → enteropathy-associated T-cell lymphoma, small-bowel adenocarcinoma
Dapsone → hemolysis/methemoglobinemia; restrictive diet → nutritional imbalance

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Follow **symptoms, nutritional labs, anti-tTG trend**; persistent elevation suggests gluten exposure
Bone-density assessment in adults with risk/malabsorption; test symptomatic first-degree relatives
No proven primary prevention; do not start gluten exclusion before diagnostic testing

rows.label: Mimics
items: IBS: no objective malabsorption, anemia, or inflammatory injury
Giardiasis: contaminated water exposure, stool antigen/PCR positive
Pancreatic insufficiency: low fecal elastase, pancreatic risk history

chlamydia-infection.name: Chlamydia infection
chlamydia-infection.scope: Chlamydia trachomatis, nongonococcal urethritis, cervicitis, lymphogranuloma venereum, neonatal conjunctivitis and pneumonia, NAAT screening and diagnosis, doxycycline and azithromycin
chlamydia-infection.core: Often silent sexually transmitted intracellular infection causing urethritis or cervicitis; untreated infection threatens fertility and can infect newborns during delivery.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Age <25 years, new/multiple partners, inconsistent condom use, infected partner; perinatal exposure

rows.label: Clues
items: Dysuria, scant discharge, sterile pyuria; friable cervix, mucopurulent discharge, postcoital bleeding
★ Neonatal conjunctivitis at **5–12 days**; afebrile staccato pneumonia at **1–3 months**
LGV: transient painless genital ulcer → tender inguinal nodes/buboes or invasive proctocolitis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: C. trachomatis: obligate intracellular bacterium; D–K serovars cause genital/perinatal infection, L1–L3 cause LGV

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **NAAT**: vaginal swab preferred in women; first-catch urine in men; rectal swab after exposure
Test for gonorrhea, HIV, syphilis; fever/pelvic pain → evaluate for PID
Infant conjunctival testing requires epithelial cells; nasopharyngeal testing for pneumonia
Sexually active MSM: annual site-specific screening; every 3–6 months with persistent high risk

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Uncomplicated infection → **doxycycline for 7 days**; LGV → 21 days
★ Pregnancy → **azithromycin**, single dose; alternative when adherence doubtful, less reliable for rectal infection
Neonatal disease → oral erythromycin for 14 days; azithromycin alternative; topical treatment alone inadequate
Gonorrhea suspected or detected → add ceftriaxone; PID requires broader multidrug coverage

rows.label: Complications
items: PID → tubal infertility, ectopic pregnancy, chronic pelvic pain; epididymitis, reactive arthritis
LGV → rectal strictures/fistulas; infant macrolides → hypertrophic pyloric stenosis risk

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Treat partners from preceding **60 days**; expedited partner treatment where legal
Abstain until 7-day course completed or 7 days after single dose, and partners treated
Annual screening: sexually active women <25 years, older women with risk; pregnancy entry screening, risk-based rescreening
Retest at 3 months; pregnancy test-of-cure at 4 weeks; neonatal eye ointment does not prevent chlamydia

rows.label: Mimics
items: Gonorrhea: often more purulent; organism-specific NAAT differentiates
M. genitalium: persistent nongonococcal urethritis after doxycycline; separate NAAT
HSV: painful ulcers and external dysuria rather than isolated cervical discharge

chronic-kidney-disease.name: Chronic kidney disease and end-stage renal disease
chronic-kidney-disease.scope: CKD progression, anemia of CKD (erythropoietin deficiency), mineral and bone disorder, uremic complications, volume overload, indications for emergent dialysis (AEIOU), vascular access
chronic-kidney-disease.core: Persistent kidney injury or reduced filtration causes progressive cardiovascular, metabolic and uremic complications; dialysis follows clinical indications rather than creatinine alone.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Diabetes, hypertension, glomerular disease, obstruction, recurrent AKI, inherited cystic disease
NSAIDs, smoking and uncontrolled proteinuria accelerate progression

rows.label: Clues
items: Early disease often asymptomatic; advanced disease → fatigue, pruritus, anorexia, edema
Uremia: confusion, pericardial friction rub, nausea or bleeding despite normal platelet count
Labs: normocytic anemia, hyperkalemia, metabolic acidosis, ↑phosphate, low/normal calcium

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Nephron loss → hyperfiltration in remaining nephrons, proteinuria and fibrosis
↓Erythropoietin causes anemia; phosphate retention/↓calcitriol → secondary hyperparathyroidism and renal bone disease

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **eGFR <60** or kidney-damage markers for **≥3 months** establishes CKD
Urine albumin/creatinine ratio, urinalysis, creatinine trend; ultrasound for size/obstruction
Stage by GFR and albuminuria; small echogenic kidneys support chronicity but are not universal
Monitor CBC, ferritin/TSAT, K, bicarbonate, calcium, phosphate and PTH

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Albuminuric CKD → **ACE inhibitor/ARB**; monitor creatinine/K; never combine both
SGLT2 inhibitor for T2DM or qualifying albuminuric CKD/HF, generally starting eGFR ≥20
Overload → salt restriction, furosemide; high phosphate → sevelamer; selected severe hyperparathyroidism → calcitriol
Iron repletion before ESA for selected persistent anemia; correct clinically significant metabolic acidosis
★ **Dialysis (AEIOU)**: refractory acidosis/hyperkalemia/overload, dialyzable toxins, uremic complications

rows.label: Complications
items: Cardiovascular death, fractures, severe hyperkalemic arrhythmia, malnutrition
Dialysis access infection/thrombosis; rapid urea reduction → dialysis disequilibrium

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Preserve arm veins; plan **AV fistula** before hemodialysis; temporary catheter for emergencies; early transplant referral
BP/glycemic control, avoid nephrotoxins, renal drug adjustment; hepatitis B vaccination before dialysis

rows.label: Mimics
items: AKI: acute creatinine change; may complicate established CKD
Prerenal azotemia: reversible perfusion deficit without persistent structural injury

chronic-lymphocytic-leukemia.name: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia
chronic-lymphocytic-leukemia.scope: Asymptomatic lymphocytosis, smudge cells, flow cytometry (CD5/CD19/CD20/CD23), Rai/Binet staging, hypogammaglobulinemia, autoimmune hemolytic anemia, Richter transformation
chronic-lymphocytic-leukemia.core: An older adult with persistent clonal mature B-cell lymphocytosis may have indolent CLL requiring observation rather than immediate treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Older age, male sex, family history; frequently discovered incidentally on CBC

rows.label: Clues
items: Painless lymphadenopathy, splenomegaly; smear with small mature lymphocytes and **smudge cells**
Recurrent sinopulmonary infection suggests hypogammaglobulinemia
★ Rapid asymmetric node growth, fever, weight loss and ↑LDH → **Richter transformation**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Accumulation of dysfunctional clonal B lymphocytes in blood, marrow and lymphoid tissue
Immune dysregulation causes antibody deficiency and autoimmune cytopenias

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Flow cytometry**: clonal B cells coexpress **CD5/CD19/CD23**, weak CD20 and surface immunoglobulin
Clonal B-cell count **≥5000/µL for ≥3 months** supports CLL; lower count without disease → MBL
Smudge cells alone not diagnostic; nodal disease with lower circulating count → SLL
CBC, examination, hemolysis studies/DAT for anemia; marrow biopsy not routinely needed for diagnosis
Before treatment: assess TP53/del(17p), IGHV and TLS risk; suspected transformation → node biopsy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Asymptomatic early disease → **watchful waiting** with clinical/CBC follow-up
Progressive marrow failure, bulky symptomatic disease, B symptoms or refractory autoimmune cytopenias → treatment
**Acalabrutinib/zanubrutinib** or venetoclax + obinutuzumab; regimen chosen by genetics/comorbidity
Autoimmune hemolytic anemia → glucocorticoids; severe recurrent infections with low IgG → selected IVIG
Venetoclax → gradual escalation with tumor-lysis prevention and monitoring

rows.label: Complications
items: Bacterial infections, warm autoimmune hemolysis, immune thrombocytopenia, second cancers
BTK inhibitors → bleeding/atrial arrhythmia; anti-CD20 drugs → HBV reactivation

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Vaccinate before immunosuppression; avoid live vaccines during significant immunocompromise
Screen HBV before anti-CD20 treatment; skin surveillance and routine cancer screening

rows.label: Mimics
items: Reactive lymphocytosis: transient, polyclonal cells
Mantle cell lymphoma: CD5-positive but usually CD23-negative, cyclin D1-positive

congenital-heart-disease.name: Congenital heart disease
congenital-heart-disease.scope: Cyanotic heart disease (5 Ts: Tetralogy of Fallot, TGA, truncus, tricuspid atresia, TAPVR), acyanotic heart disease (VSD, ASD, PDA, coarctation of aorta), hyperoxia test, prostaglandin E1
congenital-heart-disease.core: Neonatal cyanosis or shock as the ductus closes demands urgent assessment for duct-dependent congenital heart disease.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Maternal diabetes, congenital rubella, family history; Down syndrome → AV septal defects
Prematurity → PDA; Turner syndrome → coarctation

rows.label: Clues
items: Poor feeding, diaphoresis, tachypnea, hepatomegaly → infant heart failure
VSD: harsh holosystolic lower-left sternal murmur; ASD: **fixed split S2**
PDA: continuous machinery murmur, bounding pulses; coarctation: weak femoral pulses, arm–leg BP gradient

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Left-to-right shunts increase pulmonary flow; longstanding vascular remodeling can reverse flow → Eisenmenger syndrome
Duct-dependent lesions require pulmonary/systemic flow or mixing through fetal communications

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Preductal/right-hand and postductal/foot oxygen saturation; **echocardiography** defines anatomy
★ Hyperoxia test: little PaO2 rise with 100% oxygen suggests cardiac shunting; echo preferred
ECG and chest radiograph support diagnosis; normal murmur does not exclude critical disease

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Suspected duct-dependent lesion → **prostaglandin E1** immediately; monitor for apnea
★ Tet spell → knee–chest position, oxygen, fluids, morphine; refractory → phenylephrine or propranolol
TGA with inadequate mixing → balloon atrial septostomy, then arterial switch
Large shunts → diuretics, closure; premature PDA → ibuprofen; **obstructed TAPVR → emergency repair**
Coarctation → repair; irreversible Eisenmenger physiology → **do not close shunt**

rows.label: Complications
items: Pulmonary hypertension, failure to thrive, arrhythmias, infective endocarditis
Right-to-left shunting → brain abscess, paradoxical emboli, secondary erythrocytosis

rows.label: Prevention
items: Pulse-ox newborn screening; rubella immunization before pregnancy; maternal glycemic control
Endocarditis prophylaxis for selected unrepaired cyanotic or prosthetic-material lesions during dental procedures

rows.label: Mimics
items: Lung disease: substantial oxygen response, pulmonary findings
PPHN: elevated pulmonary resistance with structurally normal heart

table.title: Five cyanotic lesions
rows: RV obstruction, VSD, overriding aorta, RVH; boot-shaped heart
Parallel circuits; single S2; egg-on-string silhouette
Pulmonary veins drain systemically; obstruction → edema

congenital-heart-disease.evidence: Not checked online; established pediatric cardiology teaching.

copd.name: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
copd.scope: Stable COPD, acute exacerbation (AECOPD), oxygen-induced hypercapnia, noninvasive ventilation (NIV/BiPAP), indications for intubation, bronchodilators and glucocorticoids
copd.core: Persistent airflow obstruction after inhalational exposure causes progressive exertional dyspnea and episodic infectious or inflammatory exacerbations.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Tobacco, biomass smoke, occupational dusts; alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency with early/basilar emphysema

rows.label: Clues
items: Chronic cough/sputum, prolonged expiration, wheeze, hyperinflation
★ **Somnolence, exhaustion, silent chest, worsening acidosis** → impending respiratory failure

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Small-airway inflammation + alveolar destruction → expiratory collapse, air trapping, impaired diffusion
Excess oxygen worsens CO₂ retention mainly through V/Q mismatch and Haldane effect

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Postbronchodilator FEV₁/FVC <0.70** confirms persistent obstruction in compatible clinical setting
Exacerbation: pulse oximetry; ABG for severe distress/altered mentation; radiograph for pneumonia, edema, pneumothorax
Consider ECG, troponin, BNP, or PE evaluation when symptoms exceed expected exacerbation pattern

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Exacerbation → **albuterol + ipratropium**, prednisone for 5 days; titrate oxygen to 88–92%
Antibiotics: purulence + increased dyspnea/sputum volume, or ventilatory support; doxycycline/azithromycin options
★ Hypercapnic acidosis, pH ≤7.35 → **BiPAP** unless aspiration risk, arrest, instability, inability to cooperate
Intubate for failed NIV, severe encephalopathy, refractory hypoxemia, or inability to protect airway
Long-term oxygen if stable PaO₂ ≤55 or saturation ≤88%; selected cor pulmonale/polycythemia with PaO₂ 56–59

rows.label: Complications
items: Pulmonary hypertension, cor pulmonale, secondary polycythemia, cachexia
Pneumonia risk with inhaled steroids; ventilation → dynamic hyperinflation, auto-PEEP, barotrauma

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Smoking cessation**, influenza/COVID/pneumococcal/RSV vaccination when eligible, pulmonary rehabilitation
Check inhaler technique/adherence; offer alpha-1 antitrypsin testing at least once

rows.label: Mimics
items: Asthma: variable symptoms and reversible obstruction
Heart failure: orthopnea, edema, vascular congestion; bronchiectasis: copious sputum, dilated bronchi

table.title: Stable inhaled treatment
rows: Exacerbations with eosinophilia or concurrent asthma

copd.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [GOLD 2026](https://goldcopd.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/GOLD-REPORT-2026-v1.3-8Dec2025_WMV2.pdf); acute ventilatory care: established teaching.

dermatophyte-infections.name: Dermatophyte infections
dermatophyte-infections.scope: Tinea capitis, tinea corporis, tinea pedis, tinea cruris, onychomycosis, potassium hydroxide preparation, oral and topical antifungals
dermatophyte-infections.core: Keratin-invading fungi cause scaly skin lesions or infected hair/nails; the anatomic site determines topical versus systemic treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Warm humid conditions, occlusive footwear, shared showers, wrestling, infected animals or contacts
Diabetes, immunosuppression; childhood favors scalp infection; nail disease increases with age

rows.label: Clues
items: Pruritus and peripheral scaling; steroid exposure may distort borders and suppress inflammation
★ **Boggy tender scalp plaque** → kerion; inflammatory disease risks permanent scarring alopecia
Interdigital maceration/fissures can become bacterial entry sites

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Trichophyton, Microsporum, Epidermophyton digest keratin in stratum corneum, hair, and nails
Follicular/deep involvement prevents topical agents from reaching the infected reservoir

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **KOH preparation of active edge** → branching septate hyphae; obtain before systemic treatment when uncertain
Scalp: hair/plucked scale microscopy and culture; nail: clipping KOH, PAS, or fungal culture
Wood lamp detects only selected organisms; negative fluorescence does not exclude tinea
Refractory/widespread infection → reassess diagnosis, adherence, resistance; fungal culture can guide further care

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Limited skin disease → **topical terbinafine** or clotrimazole; continue beyond clinical clearing
★ Hair infection → **oral griseofulvin or terbinafine**; adjunct selenium sulfide/ketoconazole shampoo reduces spread
Nail infection → confirm fungus, then oral terbinafine; baseline liver assessment; counsel slow regrowth
Avoid topical corticosteroid monotherapy or steroid-antifungal combinations; extensive disease may require oral antifungal

rows.label: Complications
items: Secondary cellulitis, persistent nail dystrophy, recurrent infection from untreated reservoirs
Oral antifungals: hepatotoxicity, drug interactions; griseofulvin contraindicated during pregnancy

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Keep feet dry**, change socks, avoid shared towels/combs, disinfect sports gear
Treat symptomatic contacts/pets and coexisting foot disease; avoid barefoot communal-shower exposure

rows.label: Mimics
items: Candida intertrigo: satellite pustules, scrotal involvement
Psoriasis: sharply demarcated plaques, nail pitting; alopecia areata: smooth nonscaly patches

table.title: Site clues
rows: Broken hairs, black dots, patchy alopecia
Annular plaque, advancing border, central clearing
Thick yellow brittle nail, subungual debris

dermatophyte-infections.evidence: Not checked online; established dermatophyte diagnosis and site-based treatment.

diverticular-disease.name: Diverticular disease
diverticular-disease.scope: Diverticulosis, acute diverticulitis, complicated diverticulitis (abscess, perforation, fistula), CT imaging, antibiotic therapy
diverticular-disease.core: Diverticulosis can bleed without pain; inflamed diverticula cause focal abdominal pain, with CT distinguishing uncomplicated disease from abscess or perforation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Older age, obesity, smoking, low physical activity; regular NSAID use
Immunosuppression increases severity and can blunt fever or peritoneal findings

rows.label: Clues
items: Left lower quadrant tenderness, fever, leukocytosis, altered bowel habits
★ **Pneumaturia, fecaluria, recurrent polymicrobial UTI** → colovesical fistula
Peritoneal signs, hypotension, persistent vomiting → complicated disease requiring hospital evaluation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Mucosa/submucosa herniate through muscular weak points at penetrating vessels
Diverticular inflammation causes localized microperforation; adjacent vessel erosion causes arterial bleeding

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Suspected first/severe episode → **CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast**
Colonic wall thickening and pericolic stranding support inflammation; assess abscess, free air, obstruction
★ **Avoid colonoscopy during acute inflammation**; perforation risk
Colonoscopy after recovery for complicated disease, alarm findings, or overdue cancer screening; usually wait 6–8 weeks

rows.label: Tx
items: Low-risk uncomplicated disease: oral hydration, analgesia, advance diet as symptoms improve; antibiotics selective
★ Frail, immunocompromised, systemically ill, or complicated → **antibiotics** covering gram-negatives/anaerobes
Outpatient option: amoxicillin-clavulanate; hospitalized severe disease: IV ceftriaxone + metronidazole
Small abscess: antibiotics; larger accessible abscess, often >3 cm → percutaneous drainage
★ Peritonitis, uncontrolled sepsis, obstruction → **urgent surgery**; fistula → elective resection after stabilization

rows.label: Complications
items: Abscess, free perforation, stricture, fistula; recurrence does not automatically require colectomy
Severe diverticular hemorrhage may require colonoscopic hemostasis or angiographic embolization

rows.label: Prevention
items: Fiber-rich diet after recovery, exercise, weight management, smoking cessation
No need to avoid nuts, seeds, popcorn; avoid regular NSAIDs when possible

rows.label: Mimics
items: Colon cancer: progressive symptoms, weight loss, iron deficiency; can coexist
Ischemic colitis: sudden cramping then hematochezia, vascular risk
IBS: recurrent pain without fever or objective inflammation

essential-hypertension.name: Essential hypertension
essential-hypertension.scope: Blood pressure staging, nonpharmacologic interventions (weight loss, DASH, exercise), first-line antihypertensive agents, resistant hypertension
essential-hypertension.core: Persistently elevated arterial pressure usually reflects multifactorial primary hypertension; confirm accurate repeated measurements before long-term treatment decisions.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Age, family history, obesity, excess sodium/alcohol, inactivity, poor sleep
NSAIDs, stimulants, oral contraceptives can raise BP; assess before labeling primary disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Usually asymptomatic; headache alone does not establish hypertensive emergency
★ **Acute target-organ injury** with severe pressure → hypertensive emergency; BP number alone insufficient

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Increased vascular resistance, altered renal sodium handling, sympathetic/RAAS activation sustain elevated pressure
Chronic endothelial injury accelerates atherosclerosis and small-vessel organ damage

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Average ≥2 readings on ≥2 visits; confirm using **home BP or ambulatory monitoring**
Rest seated, feet supported, correct cuff, arm at heart level; avoid recent caffeine/exercise
BMP, creatinine/eGFR, urinalysis/albuminuria, lipids, glucose/A1c, ECG assess risk and injury
Resistant: above goal on 3 agents including diuretic, or controlled on ≥4; exclude pseudoresistance

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **DASH diet, weight reduction, sodium restriction, aerobic activity**, moderate alcohol; target generally <130/80
≥140/90 → drugs, usually two classes; ≥130/80 with CVD, diabetes, CKD, or PREVENT ≥7.5% → drugs
★ Low-risk stage 1: **3–6 months lifestyle**, then drugs if still ≥130/80; updated 2025 threshold
Initial: chlorthalidone, amlodipine, lisinopril, or losartan; albuminuric CKD → ACE inhibitor/ARB
Resistant after optimized triple regimen → spironolactone; monitor K/creatinine; never combine ACE inhibitor + ARB

rows.label: Complications
items: Stroke, MI, LV hypertrophy/HF, CKD, retinopathy, aortic disease
Thiazide: low Na/K, gout; ACE inhibitor: cough/angioedema; RAAS drugs contraindicated in pregnancy

rows.label: Prevention
items: Medication adherence, home readings, regular follow-up; assess orthostatic symptoms in older adults

rows.label: Mimics
items: White-coat hypertension: office high, home normal
Masked hypertension: elevated out-of-office only; secondary causes: abrupt/refractory pressure with renal/endocrine clues

gallstone-disease.name: Gallstone disease
gallstone-disease.scope: Biliary colic, acute cholecystitis, choledocholithiasis, cholangitis, gallstone pancreatitis
gallstone-disease.core: Gallstone location determines the syndrome: transient cystic obstruction, gallbladder inflammation, common-duct obstruction/infection, or pancreatic inflammation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Age, female sex, pregnancy, obesity, rapid weight loss, ileal disease/resection
Hemolysis/cirrhosis → pigment stones; critical illness/TPN → acalculous cholecystitis

rows.label: Clues
items: Postprandial RUQ/epigastric discomfort radiating to back or right shoulder; assess fever and jaundice
★ **Fever + RUQ pain + jaundice** → cholangitis; hypotension/confusion → severe infection
Pancreatitis: persistent epigastric pain radiating to back, vomiting; ALT >150 supports biliary cause

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Cholesterol supersaturation or pigment precipitation creates calculi; obstruction location dictates organ injury
Infected obstructed bile ducts require drainage because antibiotics cannot reliably sterilize a closed system

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **RUQ ultrasound first**; CBC, bilirubin/alkaline phosphatase, AST/ALT, lipase
Suspected cholecystitis with equivocal ultrasound → HIDA; nonvisualized gallbladder supports cystic-duct obstruction
Intermediate common-duct stone probability → MRCP or EUS; ERCP reserved primarily for treatment
★ Direct intervention: **stone seen, cholangitis, or bilirubin >4 mg/dL plus dilated duct**

rows.label: Tx
items: Analgesia, fluids, antiemetics; infection → ceftriaxone/metronidazole or piperacillin/tazobactam
★ **Cholangitis → urgent biliary drainage**, immediately after stabilization if shock; do not await antibiotic response
Poor surgical candidate with acute cholecystitis → percutaneous cholecystostomy
★ Gallstone pancreatitis → supportive care, early oral feeding; **no urgent ERCP without cholangitis/persistent obstruction**

rows.label: Complications
items: Empyema, gangrene, perforation, abscess, septic shock; pancreatitis → necrosis/organ failure
Cholecystoenteric fistula → gallstone ileus; imaging: bowel obstruction, pneumobilia, ectopic stone
ERCP → pancreatitis/bleeding/perforation; cholecystectomy → bile-duct injury

rows.label: Prevention
items: Maintain healthy weight; avoid rapid weight loss; selected bariatric patients → ursodiol prophylaxis
After duct clearance → cholecystectomy; after mild biliary pancreatitis → same-admission cholecystectomy
Asymptomatic uncomplicated stones → observation; no routine prophylactic surgery

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hepatitis: marked aminotransferase elevation, no obstructing stone
PUD: burning epigastric pain, ulcer on endoscopy
Inferior MI: ischemic ECG/troponin changes, cardiovascular risk

table.title: Localizing obstruction
rows: Persistent >6 hours, Murphy sign, wall thickening
Cholestatic labs, duct stone/dilation; no infection
ERCP extraction or operative duct clearance
Inflamed gallbladder without stones; critically ill

gastroesophageal-reflux-disease.name: Gastroesophageal reflux disease
gastroesophageal-reflux-disease.scope: Clinical diagnosis, empiric PPI trial, lifestyle measures, alarm symptoms, Barrett esophagus screening, 24-hour pH monitoring
gastroesophageal-reflux-disease.core: Heartburn and acid regurgitation after meals or recumbency suggest reflux; complications or diagnostic uncertainty change the testing pathway.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Obesity, pregnancy, hiatal hernia, smoking; drugs reducing lower esophageal sphincter tone
Late large meals and individual food triggers exacerbate symptoms

rows.label: Clues
items: Sour taste, nocturnal symptoms, chest discomfort; chronic cough/hoarseness nonspecific and often multifactorial
★ **Dysphagia, odynophagia, bleeding, weight loss**, persistent vomiting, anemia → endoscopy
Exertional or acute chest pain requires cardiac evaluation before attributing symptoms to reflux

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Transient lower sphincter relaxation and impaired barrier allow gastric contents into esophagus
Acid exposure → erosions; chronic injury may produce intestinal metaplasia

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Typical symptoms without alarms → **8-week empiric once-daily PPI trial**
Alarm features or failed treatment → upper endoscopy; biopsies evaluate alternative mucosal disease
★ Unproven GERD + normal endoscopy → **ambulatory pH monitoring off PPI**
Proven GERD with refractory symptoms → impedance-pH testing on PPI after optimizing use
Manometry evaluates motility and precedes antireflux surgery; not the primary reflux diagnostic test

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Omeprazole 30–60 minutes before breakfast**; verify adherence before escalation
Intermittent mild symptoms → antacid or famotidine; persistent breakthrough → optimize/split PPI schedule
Weight reduction if overweight; avoid meals within 2–3 hours of bedtime, elevate bed head
Objective reflux with troublesome regurgitation despite optimized drugs → fundoplication or selected endoscopic intervention
Severe erosive esophagitis → long-term PPI or surgery; step down uncomplicated controlled disease

rows.label: Complications
items: Erosive esophagitis, peptic stricture, Barrett esophagus, adenocarcinoma
Stricture → endoscopic dilation plus acid suppression; dysplastic Barrett requires specialist eradication treatment

rows.label: Prevention
items: Barrett screening: chronic reflux + ≥3 additional risks: male, >50, White, tobacco, obesity, first-degree family history
Smoking cessation and symptom-directed trigger reduction; routine endoscopy unnecessary for every reflux patient

rows.label: Mimics
items: Achalasia: solids and liquids dysphagia, impaired sphincter relaxation
Eosinophilic esophagitis: atopy, food impaction, eosinophilic biopsy
Functional heartburn: normal reflux burden and no symptom association

gastroesophageal-reflux-disease.evidence: Not checked online; established ACG reflux and Barrett screening teaching.

gout.name: Gout and crystal arthropathy
gout.scope: Acute gout, chronic gout and urate lowering, pseudogout (CPPD)
gout.core: Abrupt intensely painful inflammatory arthritis from crystal deposition; gout and CPPD require different long-term prevention despite similar flare management.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Gout: CKD, obesity, alcohol, purines/fructose, thiazide/loop diuretics, low-dose aspirin
CPPD: older age, joint injury, hyperparathyroidism, hemochromatosis, hypomagnesemia
Flares follow surgery, dehydration, illness, or changes in urate concentration

rows.label: Clues
items: Rapid-onset red swollen tender joint, often overnight; fever possible
Chronic gout: tophi on ears/olecranon, erosive arthritis; recurrent flares separated by asymptomatic intervals
CPPD in younger adults → investigate associated metabolic disorders

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Crystal phagocytosis activates inflammasome/IL-1 → neutrophilic synovitis
Most hyperuricemia reflects reduced renal urate excretion rather than excessive production

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ First/atypical acute monoarthritis → **arthrocentesis**, polarized microscopy, Gram stain/culture
★ **Crystals do not exclude septic arthritis**; serum urate may be normal during gout flare
Chronic imaging: punched-out defects with overhanging edges; ultrasound double-contour sign supports urate deposition

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Acute either crystal flare → **NSAID, colchicine, or glucocorticoid**; intraarticular steroid only after infection excluded
CKD/ulcer/anticoagulation → favor steroid; adjust colchicine for renal impairment/interactions; avoid NSAIDs in advanced CKD
★ Urate lowering: **allopurinol first-line**, including CKD; start low, titrate to serum urate <6 mg/dL
Continue urate lowering during flares; may start during treated flare; no routine asymptomatic-hyperuricemia treatment

rows.label: Complications
items: Gout: destructive arthritis, uric-acid stones; CPPD: chronic degenerative/inflammatory arthropathy
Allopurinol hypersensitivity; colchicine → diarrhea/neuromyopathy
Xanthine-oxidase inhibitors + azathioprine/6-MP → severe marrow suppression

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Urate lowering: **tophi, joint damage, ≥2 flares/year**; first flare with CKD ≥3/stones/urate >9 → consider
Starting urate lowering → colchicine/NSAID prophylaxis 3–6 months; serial urate monitoring
Weight reduction, limit alcohol/fructose; replace thiazide with losartan when feasible; retain indicated aspirin
Before allopurinol: HLA-B*58:01 testing with Southeast Asian/African American ancestry; CPPD lacks crystal-depleting drugs

rows.label: Mimics
items: Septic arthritis: positive culture, bacteremia risk; aspiration essential when uncertain
Cellulitis: superficial inflammation, less restriction of passive joint motion
RA: persistent symmetric small-joint synovitis

gout.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [ACR gout guideline 2020](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10563586/), [ACR gout education 2025](https://rheumatology.org/patients/gout); CPPD established teaching.

hypercalcemia.name: Hypercalcemia
hypercalcemia.scope: Primary hyperparathyroidism, malignancy-associated hypercalcemia, milk-alkali syndrome, IV saline resuscitation, calcitonin, bisphosphonates
hypercalcemia.core: Elevated calcium causes stones, constipation, polyuria, weakness, and neuropsychiatric changes; PTH distinguishes hormone-driven disease from other causes.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Parathyroid adenoma/hyperplasia, malignancy, prolonged immobilization
Thiazides, lithium, excess vitamin D or calcium/absorbable alkali, granulomatous disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Dehydration, nausea, abdominal pain, reduced reflexes; ECG may show shortened QT
★ **Calcium >14 mg/dL**, confusion, arrhythmia, or severe volume depletion → urgent treatment
Primary hyperparathyroidism often asymptomatic; malignancy-associated disease tends to progress rapidly

rows.label: Pathophys
items: PTH promotes bone resorption and renal calcium retention while increasing phosphate excretion
Hypercalcemia impairs renal concentration → dehydration, reduced calcium clearance, self-reinforcing elevation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Confirm with repeat total/albumin-adjusted or **ionized calcium**, especially with altered proteins or critical illness
★ **Intact PTH first**; elevated or inappropriately normal → PTH-dependent
Suppressed PTH → PTHrP, vitamin D metabolites, malignancy/myeloma evaluation guided by context
Primary disease versus FHH → urine calcium; clearance ratio <0.01 favors FHH, with overlap
Parathyroid imaging localizes before surgery; never establishes biochemical diagnosis

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Severe/symptomatic → **IV isotonic saline**, then calcitonin for rapid temporary lowering
★ **IV zoledronic acid** for sustained malignancy control; denosumab if severe renal limitations/refractory disease
Calcitriol-mediated disease → glucocorticoids; dialysis for refractory life-threatening elevation or inability to hydrate
Primary disease: surgery for symptoms, age <50, calcium >1 above ULN, osteoporosis/fracture, stones, eGFR <60
Stop causative supplements/drugs; loop diuretic only for fluid overload, not routine calcium elimination

rows.label: Complications
items: Nephrolithiasis, nephrocalcinosis, AKI, osteoporosis/fractures, pancreatitis
Calcitonin tachyphylaxis after 48–72 hours; antiresorptives can cause hypocalcemia

rows.label: Prevention
items: Hydration, avoid excess calcium/alkali; monitor calcium, renal function, and bone density when observing primary disease

rows.label: Mimics
items: FHH: lifelong mild elevation, family history, hypocalciuria; surgery ineffective
Pseudohypercalcemia: high protein-bound calcium but normal ionized fraction

hypercalcemia.evidence: Not checked online; established calcium evaluation and emergency management.

hyperglycemic-crises.name: Hyperglycemic crises
hyperglycemic-crises.core: Insulin-deficient diabetes with osmotic diuresis: rapid acidotic illness or slowly progressive hyperosmolar encephalopathy.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Infection, missed insulin, pump failure, MI; DKA often type 1, HHS often older type 2
Euglycemic triggers: **SGLT2 inhibitors**, pregnancy, fasting

rows.label: Clues
items: Polyuria, thirst, weight loss, dry mucosa, tachycardia
DKA: abdominal pain, vomiting, **Kussmaul breathing**; HHS: profound dehydration, focal deficits
★ Severe: **hypotension, stupor**, or coma → ICU

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Insulin deficit + counterregulatory hormones → lipolysis, ketogenesis; residual insulin in HHS limits ketosis
Total-body K depleted despite initially normal/high serum K

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Glucose, electrolytes, venous pH, β-hydroxybutyrate**, osmolality; ECG + trigger evaluation
Effective osmolality = 2 × Na + glucose/18; glucose in mg/dL
★ HHS: **effective osmolality >300 OR total >320 mOsm/kg**; substantial ketosis/acidosis → mixed DKA/HHS
DKA resolution: ketones <0.6 mmol/L AND (pH ≥7.3 OR HCO₃ ≥18); urine ketones/anion gap misleading

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **IV isotonic crystalloid → K correction → IV regular insulin**; K <3.5 mmol/L → delay insulin
Replace K when <5 mmol/L; glucose checks every 1–2 h, electrolytes/pH/ketones every 4 h
★ Add **dextrose** below glucose 250; euglycemic presentation → immediately; continue insulin until crisis resolves
SC basal insulin overlaps infusion 1–2 h; bicarbonate only consider pH <7.0; HHS: slower osmolar correction

rows.label: Complications
items: AKI, thrombosis; treatment: hypoglycemia, hypokalemic arrhythmias, cerebral edema, hyperchloremic acidosis

rows.label: Prevention
items: Sick-day fluids/ketone checks; continue basal insulin; ensure supplies and early follow-up
Hold SGLT2 inhibitors during acute illness and before surgery

rows.label: Mimics
items: Alcoholic ketoacidosis: binge then poor intake; usually no diabetes
Starvation ketosis: usually milder acidosis, no marked hyperglycemia
Toxic alcohols: osmolar gap, exposure; absent substantial ketonemia

table.title: Biochemistry; ketones and HCO₃ in mmol/L

hyperthyroidism.name: Hyperthyroidism and thyrotoxicosis
hyperthyroidism.scope: Graves disease, toxic multinodular goiter, toxic adenoma, subacute thyroiditis, thyroid storm, beta-blockers, thionamides, radioactive iodine
hyperthyroidism.core: Excess circulating thyroid hormone → heat intolerance, weight loss despite appetite, tremor, and tachycardia; hormone overproduction differs from destructive release.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Autoimmune history, female sex; older age favors autonomous nodules
Iodine load, amiodarone, exogenous thyroid hormone; infection/surgery can precipitate storm

rows.label: Clues
items: Hyperreflexia, frequent stools, proximal weakness, widened pulse pressure; older adults may have apathetic presentation
★ **Thyroid storm**: fever, delirium, severe tachyarrhythmia, vomiting, heart failure; clinical diagnosis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Increased tissue metabolic activity and beta-adrenergic sensitivity explain systemic manifestations
Thionamides block thyroid peroxidase; PTU also reduces peripheral T4 → T3 conversion

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **TSH first → free T4**, total T3 if T4 normal; suppressed TSH with elevated hormones
TRAb establishes Graves; uncertain cause → radioactive iodine uptake, except pregnancy/lactation
Low uptake: thyroiditis/exogenous hormone; low thyroglobulin supports exogenous ingestion

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Symptom control: **propranolol**; caution in asthma or decompensated HF
★ Storm → ICU, cooling/fluids, beta-blockade if tolerated, **PTU → iodine ≥1 hour later**, hydrocortisone
Radioiodine contraindicated during pregnancy/lactation; significant active orbitopathy favors another definitive treatment
Compression/suspicious nodule → thyroidectomy after control; pregnancy: first-trimester PTU, later methimazole

rows.label: Complications
items: AF, embolism, osteoporosis, cardiomyopathy; radioiodine often → hypothyroidism
★ Thionamides: **fever/sore throat → stop drug, urgent CBC**; PTU → severe hepatotoxicity

rows.label: Prevention
items: Monitor free T4 early during treatment; TSH recovery lags
Smoking cessation for orbitopathy; definitive treatment before planned pregnancy when feasible

rows.label: Mimics
items: Panic disorder: episodic symptoms without thyroid biochemical abnormalities
Pheochromocytoma: paroxysmal headache, sweating, severe hypertension
Menopause: hot flashes with menstrual transition, normal thyroid testing

table.title: Etiology determines treatment
rows: Diffuse uptake; bruit, orbitopathy, pretibial myxedema
One hot nodule, suppressed surrounding tissue
NSAID; prednisone if severe; no thionamides

intracranial-hemorrhage.name: Intracranial hemorrhage
intracranial-hemorrhage.scope: Intracerebral hemorrhage, hypertensive hemorrhage, amyloid angiopathy, coagulopathy reversal, blood pressure management
intracranial-hemorrhage.core: Acute focal neurologic deficits with headache, vomiting, or depressed consciousness require immediate CT to identify intraparenchymal bleeding and guide reversal.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Chronic hypertension, older age, anticoagulants/coagulopathy, stimulant use
Vascular malformation, tumor, venous thrombosis; lobar recurrence in older adults suggests cerebral amyloid angiopathy

rows.label: Clues
items: Rapid progression, seizure, severe BP elevation; small bleeds may resemble ischemic stroke
★ Hypertensive sites: **putamen, thalamus, pons, cerebellum**; amyloid favors superficial lobar locations
Declining consciousness, asymmetric pupils, abnormal posturing → mass effect/herniation
Cerebellar injury: vomiting, severe ataxia, vertigo; rapid deterioration possible despite initially preserved alertness

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Small-artery lipohyalinosis or amyloid deposition weakens vessel walls
Expanding hematoma, intraventricular extension, and perihematomal edema cause secondary injury

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Noncontrast head CT now**; CBC/platelets, INR/PTT, renal function, glucose, medication history
CTA/vascular imaging for younger patients, atypical location, suspected malformation; repeat CT for deterioration/expansion
MRI susceptibility imaging identifies microbleeds and underlying lesions after stabilization
Do not give thrombolysis or perform LP for established parenchymal hemorrhage

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Airway, head elevation, neuro-ICU; **stop anticoagulants and reverse immediately**
★ Mild/moderate ICH, SBP 150–220 → IV **nicardipine/clevidipine**, target ~140, maintain 130–150 mm Hg
Large/severe ICH requires individualized perfusion goals; avoid abrupt excessive BP reduction or SBP <130
Cerebellar deterioration, hydrocephalus, brainstem compression, or volume ≥15 mL → **urgent surgical evacuation**
Hydrocephalus → ventricular drain; herniation → hypertonic saline/mannitol; treat seizures, no routine prophylaxis

rows.label: Complications
items: Hematoma expansion, hydrocephalus, herniation, seizures, disability, recurrent hemorrhage
★ **No routine platelet transfusion** for antiplatelet-associated ICH without emergency surgery/severe thrombocytopenia

rows.label: Prevention
items: Long-term BP control, smoking/stimulant cessation; reassess anticoagulation using recurrence and embolic risks
Intermittent pneumatic compression immediately; low-dose heparin prophylaxis after bleeding stability is documented

rows.label: Mimics
items: Ischemic stroke: no acute blood on CT; SAH: thunderclap, sulcal/cisternal blood
Hemorrhagic tumor: mass/edema pattern, enhancement; confirm with MRI

lung-cancer.name: Lung cancer
lung-cancer.scope: Non-small cell, small cell, paraneoplastic syndromes, Pancoast, screening
lung-cancer.core: Persistent cough, hemoptysis, weight loss, or a suspicious lung lesion requires tissue diagnosis and staging before treatment selection.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Smoking, radon, asbestos, occupational carcinogens, prior thoracic radiation; adenocarcinoma also occurs in never-smokers

rows.label: Clues
items: Recurrent focal pneumonia, hoarseness, clubbing, unexplained pleural effusion
★ **Pancoast tumor**: shoulder/ulnar-arm pain + ipsilateral Horner syndrome
SVC obstruction: facial swelling, neck-vein distention; cord compression or airway compromise requires urgent action

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Bronchogenic malignant transformation → local invasion, lymphatic spread, hematogenous metastasis
Ectopic hormone production and immune cross-reactivity cause paraneoplastic syndromes

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Suspicious finding → **contrast chest CT**; biopsy easiest site that establishes highest stage
Central lesion/nodes → bronchoscopy/EBUS; peripheral lesion → CT-guided biopsy; effusion → cytology
PET/CT for extracranial staging, brain MRI for selected stages/small-cell disease; pulmonary function before resection
Molecular profiling and PD-L1 guide advanced NSCLC treatment; suspicious nodes often require pathologic staging

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Early operable NSCLC → **surgical resection + nodal evaluation**; inoperable localized → stereotactic radiation
Locally advanced NSCLC → combined systemic treatment/radiation ± surgery in selected patients
Metastatic NSCLC → biomarker-directed agents or immunotherapy/chemotherapy
★ Small-cell → **platinum + etoposide**, stage-dependent radiation/immunotherapy; surgery rarely used

rows.label: Complications
items: Brain/bone/adrenal/liver metastases, malignant effusion, thrombosis, respiratory failure
Radiation pneumonitis; checkpoint inhibitors → immune pneumonitis/endocrinopathies

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ USPSTF: **annual low-dose CT**, age 50–80, ≥20 pack-years, current smoking or quit <15 years
Stop after 15 quit-years or limited curative candidacy; **ACS omits quit-time restriction**
Smoking cessation and radon mitigation; chest radiographs do not substitute for screening CT

rows.label: Mimics
items: TB/fungal granuloma: microbiologic evidence; PET uptake not specific for cancer
Hamartoma: fat/popcorn calcification; pneumonia: clinical/radiographic response to antibiotics

lung-cancer.evidence: Screening checked 2026-10-30: [USPSTF 2021](https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/recommendation/lung-cancer-screening), [ACS 2023 guideline](https://acsjournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.3322/caac.21811); treatment: established stage-based framework.

lymphoma.name: Lymphoma
lymphoma.scope: Hodgkin lymphoma (Reed-Sternberg cells, CD15/CD30, B symptoms, mediastinal mass), non-Hodgkin lymphoma (diffuse large B-cell, follicular, Burkitt, mantle cell), Ann Arbor staging, excisional lymph node biopsy
lymphoma.core: Persistent painless lymphadenopathy, splenomegaly, or constitutional symptoms require tissue diagnosis; lymphoma subtype determines urgency, staging, and treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: EBV, HIV, transplantation/immunosuppression; autoimmune disease and older age for many NHL subtypes
Hodgkin incidence peaks in young adults and older age

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **B symptoms**: unexplained fever >38 °C, drenching night sweats, >10% weight loss in 6 months
Rubbery nodes; NHL often noncontiguous/extranodal; bulky thoracic disease may cause airway or SVC obstruction
Rapidly enlarging mass, cytopenias, high LDH → aggressive disease; mediastinal disease may obstruct airway/SVC

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Clonal lymphocyte proliferation; most NHLs are B-cell derived
Classical Hodgkin: sparse malignant cells within a reactive inflammatory background

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Excisional lymph-node biopsy** preserves architecture; core if excision unsafe; FNA alone generally insufficient
Histology, immunophenotyping/flow cytometry, selected cytogenetics classify disease; PET/CT stages FDG-avid lymphoma
Ann Arbor: I one region; II same diaphragm side; III both sides; IV disseminated extranodal disease
CBC, CMP, LDH, uric acid; HIV/HBV/HCV testing before systemic treatment
Stable before biopsy → avoid glucocorticoids obscuring histology; life-threatening compression → urgent specialist management

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Early classical HL → **ABVD ± involved-site radiation**; advanced disease → nivolumab-AVD among current options
DLBCL → rituximab-based combination, commonly R-CHOP; Burkitt → urgent intensive chemotherapy with CNS-directed treatment
Asymptomatic low-burden follicular disease → observation; symptomatic/bulky disease → anti-CD20-based treatment
★ Assess tumor-lysis risk before cytotoxic treatment; hydration and **urate-lowering prophylaxis** when risk warrants

rows.label: Complications
items: Tumor lysis, marrow failure, infection, cord compression, superior vena cava syndrome
Doxorubicin → cardiomyopathy; bleomycin → lung toxicity; later infertility/secondary cancers

rows.label: Prevention
items: Anti-CD20 plus HBsAg+ or anti-HBc+ → entecavir/tenofovir prophylaxis; fertility preservation before chemotherapy
Survivorship care: cardiovascular risk, thyroid/breast surveillance after relevant radiation exposures

rows.label: Mimics
items: Reactive nodes: tender, infection-linked, regress after illness
TB lymphadenitis: granulomatous inflammation; microbiologic confirmation
Leukemia: circulating blasts or marked blood-count abnormalities; marrow evaluation

multiple-sclerosis.name: Multiple sclerosis
multiple-sclerosis.scope: Relapsing-remitting, optic neuritis, transverse myelitis, internuclear ophthalmoplegia (MLF lesion), Uhthoff phenomenon, Lhermitte sign, disease-modifying therapies
multiple-sclerosis.core: Neurologic deficits separated in location and time, often including optic neuritis, suggest inflammatory CNS demyelination.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Young adulthood, female sex, family history; EBV exposure, smoking and low vitamin D association

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Optic neuritis: **pain with eye movement**, monocular visual loss, impaired color vision, afferent pupillary defect
Internuclear ophthalmoplegia: **MLF lesion**, impaired adduction with contralateral abducting nystagmus
Uhthoff: old deficits worsen with heat; Lhermitte: neck flexion triggers electric spinal sensation
Transverse myelitis: weakness, sensory level, urinary dysfunction; acute relapse generally lasts >24 hours

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Immune-mediated oligodendrocyte/myelin injury → CNS plaques, conduction block and eventual axonal loss
Relapsing-remitting: attacks with recovery; progressive forms: accumulating disability between or without attacks

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **MRI brain/cord**: periventricular, cortical/juxtacortical, infratentorial, spinal lesions; 2024 criteria add optic nerve
Classic time dissemination: new follow-up lesion or simultaneous enhancing/nonenhancing lesions; exclude better explanation
CSF-restricted oligoclonal bands support diagnosis; revised criteria also accept kappa free-light-chain index
Atypical severe visual loss/long cord lesion → serum AQP4/MOG antibodies; revised criteria permit selected earlier diagnoses
Suspected relapse → exclude fever, UTI and metabolic triggers before escalating immunosuppression

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Disabling relapse → **high-dose methylprednisolone**; severe steroid-refractory attack → plasma exchange
★ Relapsing disease → early disease-modifying drug, e.g., **ocrelizumab**, tailored to activity and pregnancy plans
Lower-activity options include interferon-beta or glatiramer; natalizumab requires JC-virus/PML risk assessment
Baclofen for spasticity; rehabilitation, bladder care and treatment of neuropathic pain
Isolated heat/infection-related worsening → treat trigger; not automatically a new inflammatory attack

rows.label: Complications
items: Gait impairment, falls, neurogenic bladder, depression and cognitive dysfunction
Immunosuppressive treatment → infection; some agents carry PML risk

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking cessation, exercise, vaccination; review contraception/pregnancy before disease-modifying drugs

rows.label: Mimics
items: B12 deficiency: symmetric posterior-column dysfunction, macrocytosis
NMOSD: AQP4-positive, often severe attacks; some MS drugs worsen disease
Stroke: abrupt maximal deficit, vascular territory

neutropenia.name: Neutropenia
neutropenia.scope: Benign ethnic neutropenia (Duffy-null), drug-induced neutropenia, febrile neutropenia, autoimmune neutropenia, ANC thresholds, evaluation and management
neutropenia.core: Infection risk tracks the depth and duration of neutrophil depletion; fever with severe neutropenia is an antibiotic emergency.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Cytotoxic chemotherapy, marrow malignancy, viral infection, autoimmune disease, B12/folate/copper deficiency
Clozapine, methimazole, propylthiouracil, TMP–SMX and other drugs can cause agranulocytosis
Duffy-null associated neutrophil counts: stable isolated reduction without increased infection risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Oral ulcers, gingivitis, recurrent bacterial/fungal infections; inflammatory signs and pus may be absent
Cyclic mouth ulcers/infections suggest cyclic neutropenia; multiple cytopenias suggest marrow disease
Drug-associated fever or sore throat → urgent CBC, especially with antithyroid drugs

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Reduced marrow production, peripheral destruction or splenic sequestration lowers circulating neutrophils
Mucosal barrier injury plus impaired innate defense permits rapid invasive bacterial infection

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **ANC = WBC × (% neutrophils + bands)/100**; repeat CBC with differential and smear
Mild: 1000–1500/µL; moderate: 500–1000; **severe <500**; profound <100
★ Febrile neutropenia: **≥38.3°C once or ≥38.0°C for ≥1 hour**, ANC <500 or expected decline
Obtain peripheral/line blood cultures, targeted cultures and imaging without delaying antibiotics
Persistent unexplained severe counts, abnormal smear or other cytopenias → marrow evaluation

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Febrile severe neutropenia → **IV cefepime**, piperacillin–tazobactam or meropenem promptly
Add vancomycin for shock, suspected line/skin infection, pneumonia or documented resistant gram-positive infection
★ Stop culprit drug; G-CSF for selected severe/drug-related cases and high-risk chemotherapy settings
Carefully selected low-risk stable patients → oral ciprofloxacin + amoxicillin–clavulanate with reliable close follow-up
High-risk persistent fever 4–7 days → fungal evaluation and empiric **caspofungin**

rows.label: Complications
items: Pseudomonas sepsis, invasive candidiasis/aspergillosis, neutropenic enterocolitis; avoid rectal instrumentation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Hand hygiene, oral care; selected prolonged profound neutropenia → antibacterial/antifungal prophylaxis
Stable Duffy-null pattern → reassurance after excluding other causes; no unnecessary G-CSF

rows.label: Mimics
items: Lymphopenia: opportunistic infection risk with preserved ANC
Acute leukemia: blasts and additional cytopenias

osteoarthritis.name: Osteoarthritis
osteoarthritis.scope: Clinical diagnosis (Heberden/Bouchard nodes, activity-related pain), radiographic findings, nonpharmacologic therapy, oral and topical NSAIDs, injections
osteoarthritis.core: Activity-related joint pain with brief morning stiffness, crepitus and bony enlargement suggests degenerative joint disease.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Older age, obesity, prior trauma, malalignment, repetitive occupational loading
Family history, particularly hand disease; obesity affects both mechanical and metabolic risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Morning stiffness generally **<30 minutes**; pain improves with rest early in disease
Knees, hips, first carpometacarpal, DIP and PIP commonly involved; MCP usually spared
Heberden nodes: DIP; Bouchard nodes: PIP; reduced motion and varus/valgus deformity
Hip disease: groin pain with restricted internal rotation; referred pain can localize to knee

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Articular cartilage loss, subchondral remodeling and osteophytes; low-grade synovial inflammation
Joint pain arises from innervated surrounding structures rather than aneural cartilage itself

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Typical presentation → **clinical diagnosis**; imaging unnecessary for straightforward mild disease
Weight-bearing radiographs if uncertain/severe: asymmetric joint-space narrowing, osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis/cysts
★ Hot acutely swollen joint → **arthrocentesis**; do not assume OA flare
OA fluid noninflammatory: usually WBC <2000/µL; inflammatory markers generally normal

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ First-line **exercise, strengthening, weight loss**; cane contralateral to painful hip/knee
★ Knee/hand pain → **topical diclofenac**; oral NSAID if insufficient and renal/GI/CV risks acceptable
Acetaminophen for selected patients unable to use NSAIDs; duloxetine for persistent pain
Intra-articular glucocorticoid for short-term relief; avoid routine opioids and hyaluronic acid injections
Severe pain/function loss despite conservative treatment → **joint replacement**

rows.label: Complications
items: Functional limitation, falls, reduced activity and secondary deconditioning
NSAIDs → GI bleeding, AKI, fluid retention; arthroplasty → infection or VTE

rows.label: Prevention
items: Healthy weight, muscle conditioning, injury prevention; physical activity does not require complete joint rest

rows.label: Mimics
items: Rheumatoid arthritis: prolonged stiffness, boggy symmetric MCP/wrist synovitis
CPPD: acute inflammatory flares, chondrocalcinosis
Septic arthritis: fever, severe painful passive motion, positive synovial culture

osteoarthritis.evidence: Not checked online; established ACR/Arthritis Foundation principles.

palliative-and-hospice-care.name: Palliative and hospice care
palliative-and-hospice-care.scope: Hospice eligibility, pain control, goals of care, surrogate requests
palliative-and-hospice-care.core: Palliative care relieves suffering at any illness stage; hospice centers care on comfort when prognosis and patient goals support a terminal-care benefit.

rows.label: Principle
items: ★ **Patient goals and informed consent** guide intervention burdens; symptom relief remains an obligation
Proportionate opioids for pain/dyspnea ethically permissible despite foreseeable unintended risks

rows.label: Do
items: ★ Ask understanding/values → discuss prognosis → recommend a goal-concordant plan
Assess capacity; use advance directive, then authorized surrogate: substituted judgment/best interests
★ Titrate **opioids** to symptoms; add stimulant laxative for constipation, reassess sedation/respiration

rows.label: Don't
items: DNR ≠ no antibiotics, fluids, nutrition or other desired treatment
Capable patient’s informed wishes override surrogate requests
No nonbeneficial interventions; explain reasoning, offer alternatives, seek ethics review for conflict

rows.label: Exceptions
items: Refractory terminal suffering → proportional palliative sedation, specialist review and consent
Emergency, unknown preferences → stabilize while clarifying wishes; honor documented refusals

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Hospice: **≤6-month prognosis** if usual course; longer survival permits recertification
Medicare hospice election concerns terminal-illness treatment; unrelated conditions remain treatable
No DNR requirement for hospice; enrollment can be revoked if goals change

palliative-and-hospice-care.evidence: Eligibility checked 2026-10-30: [CMS hospice benefit](https://www.cms.gov/medicare/payment/fee-for-service-providers/hospice); clinical ethics: established teaching.

pancreatitis.name: Pancreatitis
pancreatitis.scope: Acute pancreatitis, chronic pancreatitis, exocrine and endocrine insufficiency
pancreatitis.core: Epigastric pain radiating to the back with pancreatic inflammation may be acute; repeated injury produces irreversible chronic insufficiency.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Gallstones, alcohol, triglycerides >1,000 mg/dL, ERCP, hypercalcemia, medications
Chronic: prolonged alcohol/tobacco exposure, genetic disease, duct obstruction, autoimmune disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Severe constant pain, vomiting, tenderness, ileus; chronic disease adds steatorrhea and weight loss
★ **Hypoxemia, hypotension, oliguria, persistent SIRS** → early monitored/ICU assessment

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Premature intrapancreatic enzyme activation → autodigestion and systemic inflammation
Chronic fibrosis destroys acinar/islet tissue; lipase may normalize despite advanced disease

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Acute diagnosis: **2 of 3**—typical pain, lipase ≥3× ULN, characteristic imaging
RUQ ultrasound evaluates gallstones; triglycerides, calcium, liver tests identify cause
Contrast CT for uncertain diagnosis, deterioration, or failure to improve after 48–72 hours; not routine immediately
Chronic: CT/MRCP shows calcification/duct changes; fecal elastase <200 supports exocrine insufficiency

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Acute: **moderate lactated Ringer resuscitation**, frequent reassessment, analgesia, electrolyte correction; avoid overload
★ **Early oral low-fat feeding** within 24–48 hours if tolerated; enteral tube feeding if unable
Biliary with cholangitis → urgent ERCP; mild gallstone disease → cholecystectomy before discharge
Sterile necrosis: no antibiotics; infected: penetrating antibiotics, delayed step-up drainage/debridement
Chronic: stop alcohol/tobacco; pancreatic enzymes, nutrition/fat-soluble vitamins, pain and diabetes management

rows.label: Complications
items: ARDS, AKI, shock, hypocalcemia; local necrosis, vascular thrombosis, hemorrhage
Pseudocyst after >4 weeks; infected collection, obstruction; chronic disease → pancreatic cancer and brittle diabetes

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Treat cause**: gallbladder removal, triglyceride control, avoid culprit drug and alcohol
Post-ERCP rectal indomethacin in eligible patients; selected pancreatic duct stenting

rows.label: Mimics
items: Perforated ulcer: rigid abdomen/free air
Mesenteric ischemia: pain-exam mismatch; MI: ischemic ECG/troponin pattern

table.title: Severity and collections
